intuition.title: Oleic acid and reversible aggregation
intuition.text: Beyond roughly 3 nm, spectra broaden without added oleic acid. Reversal after oleic-acid addition supports the authors’ aggregation interpretation. This comparison does not establish a measured surface-ligand bonding structure, nor does it assign the Figure 3 TEM size to every optical trace.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 and oleic-acid discussion

intuition.title: Growth and declining particle concentration
intuition.text: The source-derived particle concentration declines by about 72% over two hours as the distribution narrows. The authors discuss growth behavior that does not follow the simple expectation they describe for diffusion-limited growth, but explicitly leave the detailed mechanism unresolved. Optical calibrations depend on cited literature, which is unreviewed in this scope.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figure 1 and growth discussion

intuition.title: Potential scale-up is an outlook
intuition.text: Heating a mixture without rapid precursor injection could simplify process control and scaling, according to the authors. The article does not demonstrate an industrial production run, a scale-up yield, or a validated manufacturing cost.

general_background.title: A phosphine-free selenium feed has different chemistry
general_background.summary: When used as a phosphine-free feed in non-injection cadmium selenide synthesis, selenium dispersed or dissolved in octadecene has different conversion chemistry from phosphine-bound selenium. The choice of reaction medium changes the supply of growth species and can shift the balance between discrete clusters and continued growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Octadecene is not always inert
general_background.summary: Octadecene provides a weakly coordinating medium for hot solution growth, leaving the ligands more freedom to control surface binding. It can also polymerize under growth conditions, leaving an alkene-derived residue that is difficult to separate from hydrophobic nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: The Trouble with ODE: Polymerization during Nanocrystal Synthesis

general_background.title: Oleate and the nanocrystal surface
general_background.summary: Bound oleate can stabilize dispersed metal chalcogenide nanocrystals, and not all surface carboxylate need occupy the same binding environment. Displacing metal carboxylate from the surface can change surface stoichiometry as well as colloidal stability.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Ligand Exchange and the Stoichiometry of Metal Chalcogenide Nanocrystals: Spectroscopic Observation of Facile Metal-Carboxylate Displacement and Binding

general_background.title: Ligand exchange can alter surface stoichiometry
general_background.summary: A neutral donor is an L-type ligand, an anionic ligand can be X-type, and a surface-bound Lewis acid can act as Z-type. Displacing a Lewis-acidic metal carboxylate during ligand exchange can change surface stoichiometry as well as the coating.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
